sections.COMMENTS:
The Crati Valley is oriented N-S and delimited on both sides by normal faults. Some of these are recognized as active in the literature (Tansi et al., 2005; 2007). Geological and geomorphological observations (e.g: Carobene and Damiani, 1985; Molin et al., 2004; Tansi et al., 2005), such as drainage pattern, deformation of the top of the metamorphic substratum (along with the overlying Pleistocene units) and radon anomalies are consistent with the hypothesis of activity on the west-dipping faults on the eastern flank of the valley.
Six earthquakes with magnitude between 5.5 and 5.9 occurred in the Crati Valley, between 1767 and 1913, in a time span less than a couple of centuries. Minor seismicity with magnitude between 4 and 5 is also present.
We propose that this Source is located on a west-dipping extensional structure that runs approximately along the eastern side of the valley.
